_comment: Example PROTOCOL.md v1 §9.3 operating-point table. DATA, not code. Constants are wfb_ng-derived SEEDS (docs/groundwork.md); RE-DERIVE on bench (§17). NOT a validated flight table.
_table_version_note: table_version on the wire is a CRC-8 CONTENT HASH of this table's canonical serialization (§3.6), NOT this integer. This field is advisory/human only. 0x2B is this table's actual computed hash (pinned in tests/table_hash_test.cpp).

units.tx_power_level: PORTABLE power INTENT index (§10.2). NOT absolute. Each TX node resolves (adapter, mcs, level) -> an absolute qdb via that adapter's LOCAL power map. No regulatory clamp (§10.3).
units.airtime_budget_frac: fraction of wall-clock airtime this link may occupy
units.arq_deadline_ms: per importance class; iframe class longer (§4.1/§8)
units.fec_scheme: none in the base table; 'rlc256' / 'rlc256_iframe' / 'tetrys_reactive' only if §14 bench gate 2 justifies it
units.fec_overhead_frac: airtime/bitrate debited for parity (§14); 0 when fec_scheme=none

_per_adapter_power: Absolute per-MCS power is authored per physical adapter in a LOCAL file (PHY_REG_PG.txt row format, §10.2), e.g. profiles/power.<adapter>.txt — one per adapter (each has its own efuse cal/antenna). Node-local, operator-owned, not shipped here. Craft has one adapter; only ground has more.
_rungs_note: MCS 6-7 are normal high rungs the RSSI-margin promote can reach (§9.4). The wfb_ng 'reserved for probe' tag is dropped in v0 (no probe side-stream).
